inventory.description: Pure, host-testable products of Packages/VisualCore: VisualCoreMath, VisualCoreSimulation, VisualCoreScenes, VisualCoreShaderSource, VisualCoreEffectsGraph, VisualCoreDiagnostics, VisualCoreAudioDSP, VisualCorePersistence, VisualCoreParameters, VisualCoreExperience (+ VisualCoreTestSupport for test targets). iOS products of Packages/VisualCoreRendering: VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreEffects, VisualCoreUI, VisualCoreAudio, VisualCoreAutomation, VisualCoreExperienceHost. For the playground (checked 2026-11-15): VisualCoreSimulation has SeededRandom, FixedStepClock, FixedStepRunner (FixedStepSimulation, ControlStream, pause, stepOnce, run), TimeStepPolicy (clamps a step to 1/240...1/30 s), ParticleSystem with ParticleForce (gravity, drag, attractor and other fields for particles only), Collision2D with CollisionCircle and CollisionCapsule (overlap, closest point, swept circle test; added at A10-P01) and NeighbourSearch (linear-scan neighbours of steering agents); VisualCoreScenes has the 2D SceneNode tree with Primitive rect, circle, line, polygon and polyline, Primitive.contains and SceneNode.hitTest, PointerTracker, PointerVelocityTracker, TapRecognizer, DoubleTapRecognizer, LongPressRecognizer, DragRecognizer, PinchRecognizer, RotateRecognizer and GestureArbiter; VisualCoreMath has Vec2, Camera2D and NumericHygiene; VisualCoreRendering has PrimitiveRenderer; VisualCoreUI has ParameterPanel; VisualCoreExperience has ExperienceStorage and the declared quality tiers. No rigid-body dynamics exist in any framework product: no box or polygon contact generation, no impulse or constraint solver, no spring constraint, no broad phase and no chart or plot component (grep 2026-11-15). The only solver in the repository is Fluid Art Playground's app-local grid FluidSolver, which is not rigid-body dynamics.

RenderHost (@MainActor) owns the EGL display, context and surfaces over ANGLE's Metal backend (EGLDisplayProvider), the CAMetalLayer RenderView, the FrameScheduler and context generations; pause/resume, replaceScene, recreateContext, renderOffscreen and destroy; scenes implement RenderScene setup/resize/render/teardown. All EGL and GL work runs on the main thread. Physics Playground's world (bodies, forces, contacts, springs, integration) is GPU-free CPU work stepped at a fixed step on the main thread at the frame boundary; drawing reads finished state and never changes it, and no simulation runs in shaders. Physics Playground adds no EGL or GL context of its own.

ResourceRegistry creates buffers, textures, programs and render targets under a ResourceBudget and rejects stale handles after a generation change. ShaderProgram, ShaderBundle and ShaderLibrary (#include expansion with line maps) compile bundled GLSL; the vc/ library holds color, field, hash, noise, palette and sdf helpers. PrimitiveRenderer draws a 2D SceneNode tree (bodies, springs as lines or polylines, vector arrows as lines and polygons) as one batched triangle list through Camera2D; FullScreenShaderScene and the effects graph (copy, colorMatrix, blur, bloom, distort, composite, feedback, flashLimit; EffectScene, EffectRenderer) are available for decorative backgrounds and highlights only.

ExperienceSession opens, checkpoints, closes and recovers an Experience on one RenderHost, applies the quality level (QualityGovernor over the experience's QualityProfile, fed by DeviceConditions thermal state and Low Power Mode) and memory/scene-phase events; ExperienceShell adapts an ExperiencePresenter (scene, controls) to Experience; ExperienceCore is the GPU-free state with its qualityTiers; ExperienceStorage is the per-experience sandbox; ExperienceFeedback routes haptics and announcements; the one app registers experiences in ExperienceRegistry and Catalog/registrations.json (ten registered, A01-A10, checked 2026-11-15; Physics Playground joins in A11-P01 and stays unregistered and unavailable in A11-P00; scripts/check_experience_packages.py forbids unregistered targets). Physics Playground version 0.1 needs no microphone, camera, photos, motion or location; saved experiments live in its own storage, so no usage description or privacy answer changes.

XcodeGen spec project.yml for the one app (target VisualCore), package schemes via scripts/xcodebuild_package.py, app tests via scripts/xcodebuild_app.py, and scripts/release_check.py: 108 named steps listed by --list on 2026-11-15 (shared checks, package and app builds/tests, per-experience release, copy-claims and verify steps of A01-A10 on iOS 27 and 26, release audits of the one app, the seven reference regression steps and the ProjectM independence check).

Physics Playground owns its domain (the body and world model with units, static bodies, gravity, drag, integration, pause, single step, time scale and reset, the spawn/grab/pin/delete editor, vector overlays and the measured state panel, presets pendulum, spring chain and stacked objects, saved experiments, stability caps, the body budget and sleeping bodies, the spoken experiment description, educational-approximation wording and content licenses) and UI under Packages/ExperiencesCreative/PhysicsPlayground/ (Core GPU-free, CoreTests, Experience with Adapter/, ExperienceTests, Shaders, scenario-manifest.json; created in A11-P01, not present today). VisualCore owns reusable machinery: the seeded fixed-step clock, runner and step policy, Collision2D, and the rigid-body pieces to come (box contacts, impulse solver with restitution, friction and positional correction, spring constraints, broad phase; VisualCoreSimulation), 2D shapes and gestures (VisualCoreScenes, drawn by VisualCoreRendering), quality, persistence and storage (constitution Principle II, A11 section). Neon Arcade's GameSimulation and Fluid Art Playground's FluidSolver stay experience code and are not reused. ProjectM stays in the harness.

Reference pinned at d93edd1, read-only; scripts/run_reference_baseline.py lists the ordered reference steps; scripts/check_reference_clean.py checks the submodule; the 7 release-check steps run in two chunks via release_check.py --only (reference-engine-xcframework, reference-build-projectm-ios-sim, reference-clean; reference-test-anglerendering-ios27, reference-test-anglerendering-ios26, projectm-reference-ios27, projectm-reference-ios26), recorded in the A11 regression baseline document (docs/apps/physics-playground/regression-baseline.md) with the phase-start commit d3797d7c.

FixedStepClock (default 1/120 s, at most 8 steps per frame, interpolation alpha) and FixedStepRunner over a FixedStepSimulation with a ControlStream of timed commands give deterministic, frame-rate-independent stepping with pause, stepOnce and run(steps:); TimeStepPolicy clamps a variable delta to 1/240...1/30 s and counts clamped and invalid deltas; SeededRandom (SplitMix64) and SeedDerivation give reproducible streams; StateDigest fingerprints state. Particle Universe (A04), Digital Aquarium (A09) and Neon Arcade (A10) step this way; the playground's world will too, so the same document and inputs give the same result.

matrix.capability: Scene rendering: bodies, springs, ground, walls and overlays as SceneNode shapes with transform, z order, visibility and colour, batched into one triangle list per tree through Camera2D on the main thread over RenderHost
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreScenesTests/SceneGraphTests, VisualCoreRenderingTests (PrimitiveRendererTests, RenderHostTests) and VisualCoreMathTests/Camera2DTests. Every node of a tree lands in one batch; polygons are capped at 256 points and polylines at 8,192; the audit does not measure performance. Shapes are procedural, never bitmap art.

matrix.capability: Geometry: 2D vectors, rectangles, circles, lines, polygons and polylines, point-in-shape tests and hit testing of a shape tree, circle and capsule overlap, closest point and swept circle tests
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreMathTests (LinearAlgebraTests), VisualCoreScenesTests/SceneGraphTests and VisualCoreSimulationTests/Collision2DTests. Box geometry for contacts (circle-box, box-box) does not exist; that is the rigid-body row M06 (G-CONTACTS).

matrix.capability: Animation: deterministic seeded fixed-step clock with interpolation alpha, tweens and timelines, easing curves for decorative motion (the physics itself is integrated, not animated)
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreSimulationTests (FixedStepClockTests, FixedStepRunnerTests, TimelineTests) and VisualCoreMathTests (EasingTests).

matrix.capability: Shader-based effects: bundled GLSL programs, full-screen shader scenes and the effects graph (blur, bloom, colour matrix, composite, flash limit) for decorative backgrounds and highlights only; the CPU solver stays authoritative and no simulation runs in shaders
matrix.source: brainstorm: shader-based effects; constitution A11 authoritative, GPU-free physics
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreRenderingTests (ShaderProgramTests, FullScreenShaderSceneTests), VisualCoreEffectsTests (PassPixelTests, EffectRendererTests) and VisualCoreEffectsGraphTests. Version 0.1 needs no custom shader; any later bundled shader records its author and license (M18).

matrix.capability: Data visualization: plots of measured quantities (speed, energy, spring extension) over time and readable numeric values, drawn as polylines and native text without a second renderer
matrix.notes: Polylines and lines drawn in one batch (SceneGraphTests, PrimitiveRendererTests) and the native parameter panel (ParameterPanelTests) exist; no chart or plot component (axes, scaling, sampling of a quantity over time) exists in any framework product (grep 2026-11-15). Oscilloscope Studio's ScopeTrace is experience code. The playground's plots and readouts are its own over polylines and native SwiftUI text. G-OVERLAYS (app-local), A11-P03.

matrix.capability: Circles and boxes with rigid-body collision: dynamic and static (zero-mass, infinite-inertia) bodies with mass and moment of inertia in stated units; circle-circle, circle-box and box-box contact generation; an impulse solver with restitution, friction and positional correction; a broad phase
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 1: circles and boxes with rigid-body collision; constitution A11 reuse first
matrix.notes: Since A11-P02 (G-BROADPHASE closed): circle and box contacts (Contacts2D), the impulse solver with warm starting (ImpulseSolver2D) and the broad phase (BroadPhase2D) cover rigid-body collision of circles and boxes, with a resting stack bounded (Contacts2DTests, ImpulseSolver2DTests, BroadPhase2DTests); WorldSimulation uses them.

matrix.capability: Constant gravity, springs and drag: a uniform gravity vector and linear drag applied to bodies each step, spring constraints between bodies or a body and a pin with rest length, bounded stiffness and damping
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 2: constant gravity, springs and drag
matrix.notes: Since A11-P02 (G-SPRINGS closed): springs between bodies or to fixed points with stiffness and damping bounded for the tick (Springs2D, Springs2DTests); constant gravity (off, Moon, Earth) and linear and angular drag (none, low, high) act on rigid bodies in WorldSimulation.

matrix.capability: Spawn, grab, pin and delete gestures: tap to spawn a chosen body, drag to grab and throw with a bounded grab force, long press or a mode to pin, a delete mode, each with a native control alternative and gesture arbitration
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 3: spawn/grab/pin/delete gestures; constitution A11 accessibility
matrix.notes: The recognizers, arbitration, pointer tracking, hit testing and the gesture-alternative check exist and are tested (GestureTests, GestureArbiterTests, PointerTrackerTests, SceneGraphTests, GestureAlternativesTests); RenderView+Touches feeds pointer events. The editor modes, grab force and pin semantics are the playground's. G-EDITOR (app-local over the recognizers), A11-P03.

matrix.capability: Pause, single step, time scale and reset: pause stops the world, single step advances exactly one fixed step while paused, time scale changes how many fixed steps a frame runs (never the step size), reset restores the experiment's initial document
matrix.notes: Since A11-P01 (G-RIGIDBODY closed): pause, single step (one tick while paused), time scales ¼, ½, 1 and 2 as whole ticks per host step (the tick never changes) and reset are built over the shared fixed step in WorldSimulation and the adapter; the same ticks give the same world at every scale (WorldSimulationTests).

matrix.capability: Presets pendulum, spring chain and stacked objects, and saved experiments: bundled starting documents that load, run deterministically and reset, and person-made experiments saved and reopened on the device
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 5: presets pendulum, spring chain, stacked objects; manual saved experiments
matrix.notes: Per-experience storage, named libraries and parameter presets exist and are tested (ExperienceStorageTests, NamedLibraryTests, ParametersTests); the pendulum and spring chain need spring constraints (G-SPRINGS) and the stack needs box contacts with friction (G-CONTACTS), both upstream in A11-P02; the preset documents and the experiment schema are G-EXPERIMENTS (app-local over ExperienceStorage), A11-P04.

matrix.capability: Velocity and force vector overlays and the measured state panel: optional arrows (shaft line and polygon head) for velocity and force per body, a native panel of measured values (position, speed, kinetic and potential energy, spring extension) with units, and a spoken summary
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 6: velocity/force vector overlays and measured state panel
matrix.notes: Lines and polygons (SceneGraphTests, PrimitiveRendererTests), the native panel (ParameterPanelTests) and rate-limited announcements (AccessibilityPlansTests) exist; no arrow primitive, vector scaling or measured-state model exists in a framework product. G-OVERLAYS (app-local), A11-P03.

matrix.capability: Fixed step and step policy: the world advances at a fixed step independent of the frame rate with a capped catch-up, a clamped and validated frame delta, timed commands and a state digest so the same document and inputs give the same result
matrix.source: cross-cutting: fixed step and step policy; constitution A11 authoritative, GPU-free physics; manual risk 1
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreSimulationTests (FixedStepClockTests, FixedStepRunnerTests, TimeStepPolicyTests, SeededRandomTests) and VisualCoreExperienceTests/StateDigestTests. The playground's world implements FixedStepSimulation in A11-P01 (G-RIGIDBODY on M06/M09).

matrix.capability: Stability and body budget: caps on body, contact and constraint counts, solver iterations, spring stiffness for the chosen step and speeds; non-finite values rejected; sleeping bodies; an experiment that would become unstable is clamped or refused
matrix.source: cross-cutting: stability and body budget; constitution A11 stable and bounded; manual risks 1 and 3
matrix.notes: Finite-value checks (NumericHygieneTests), step clamping (TimeStepPolicyTests), a particle budget per quality level (ParticleBudgetTests) and the governor (QualityGovernorTests) exist; no body budget, sleeping bodies or stiffness and speed caps exist. The solver's own iteration and stiffness bounds come with G-CONTACTS and G-SPRINGS (A11-P02); the experience's caps, budget and sleeping are G-STABILITY (app-local), A11-P05.

matrix.capability: Persistence: settings and saved experiments as versioned documents in per-experience storage with atomic writes, migration and safe recovery from damaged or newer files
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCorePersistenceTests and VisualCoreExperienceTests (ExperienceStorageTests, SavedStateStoreTests). The experiment document schema is G-EXPERIMENTS (M10).

matrix.capability: Quality tiers and low power: quality governor fed by thermal state and Low Power Mode, declared quality tiers that lower overlay detail and draw load (never the physics step), refreshed by the session
matrix.source: cross-cutting: quality tiers and low power; constitution A11 bounded resources
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreDiagnosticsTests (QualityGovernorTests, QualityProfileTests), VisualCoreExperienceTests (QualityDeclarationTests) and VisualCoreExperienceHostTests. Core.qualityTiers must match the presenter's levels (declared at P05).

matrix.capability: Accessibility and Reduce Motion: system preferences observed, decorative motion calmed without changing the physics, flashes limited, rate-limited announcements describing the experiment for VoiceOver, a control alternative for every gesture
matrix.source: cross-cutting: accessibility and Reduce Motion; constitution A11 accessibility
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreSimulationTests (AccessibilityPreferencesTests, AccessibilityPlansTests), VisualCoreUITests (SystemAccessibilityObserverTests, AccessibilityPlayersTests) and VisualCoreExperienceTests (GestureAlternativesTests). The spoken experiment description is experience wording over AnnouncementPlanner, built with the overlays in A11-P03 (G-OVERLAYS on M11).

matrix.capability: Lifecycle and context loss: context loss, resize, background and memory warning rebuild everything from versioned CPU world state; backgrounding pauses the simulation and never fast-forwards it
matrix.source: cross-cutting: lifecycle; constitution A11 bounded resources
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreRenderingTests (RenderHostTests, ResourceRegistryTests), VisualCoreExperienceHostTests and VisualCoreSimulationTests (PlaybackStateTests); FixedStepClock caps catch-up at 8 steps per frame.

matrix.capability: Licenses and provenance: every preset, palette and shader bundled later records its author and license; only original content
matrix.source: cross-cutting: licenses; constitution A11 licenses; spec FR-A11-006
matrix.notes: Since A11-P01 (G-CONTENTLICENSES closed): every bundled material records author and license (MaterialCatalog, MIT only); LicenseAudit generates docs/apps/physics-playground/content-licenses.md and a test compares it with the catalog. LicenseInventory and AcknowledgementsView cover third-party notices.

gaps.justification: The playground's body and world model with stated units (metres, kilograms, seconds), static zero-mass bodies, constant gravity, linear drag, semi-implicit integration, pause, single step, time scale and reset are the experience's domain over VisualCore's FixedStepRunner, FixedStepClock and TimeStepPolicy (clarification 5); contacts and springs come from G-CONTACTS and G-SPRINGS. Built in A11-P01: PhysicsWorld (schema 1, units, static zero-mass bodies), WorldSimulation (gravity, drag, semi-implicit integration over the shared contacts and solver, pause, single step, time scale, drop, reset through the adapter) and WorldDiagnostics.
gaps.test: Host tests (swift test, no GPU): a body in free fall matches the analytic position within a stated tolerance for the step; static bodies never move and have zero inverse mass; drag decays speed monotonically; the same document and inputs give the same state digest; pause stops stepping, single step advances exactly one fixed step, time scale changes steps per frame but never the step size, reset restores the initial document; non-finite inputs rejected

gaps.justification: Found in A11-P00: Collision2D answers circle and capsule overlap only; no contact manifold, no circle-box or box-box contacts, no impulse solver and no broad phase exist in any framework product. Contacts, an impulse solver with restitution, friction and positional correction, and a broad phase are generic 2D machinery and belong to VisualCoreSimulation (constitution A11 reuse first, clarification 5). Moved to A11-P01 because the Phase 01 gate requires circles and boxes that collide and the two-body momentum fixture: Contacts2D (circle-circle, circle-box, box-box manifolds) and ImpulseSolver2D (sequential impulses with restitution, friction and positional correction). The broad phase and resting-stack stability are G-BROADPHASE (A11-P02).
gaps.test: Host tests (Contacts2DTests, ImpulseSolver2DTests; 25 tests): separated, touching, overlapping, nested and rotated manifolds; equal circles head-on with e = 1 exchange velocities and keep momentum within 1e-9; e = 0, static bodies unchanged, threshold, friction bound, positional correction, determinism, no non-finite output; API baseline additive; reference regression at X-A11

gaps.justification: Found in A11-P00: no spring constraint exists in any framework product; spring constraints between bodies or a body and a fixed point with rest length, bounded stiffness for the chosen step and damping are generic and belong to VisualCoreSimulation (clarification 5). Built in A11-P02: Springs2D (SpringAnchor2D, Spring2D, stable stiffness 0.1·m/dt² and damping m/dt, apply as impulses at the anchors); the world applies springs before gravity (research D1).
gaps.test: Host tests (Springs2DTests, 10 tests): ends pulled together, world anchors and static ends fixed, zero length inert, clamps exact, undamped energy within 2 % over 1,200 ticks, damped energy non-increasing and below 10 % by 10 s, equilibrium m·g/k within 2 %; API baseline additive; reference regression at X-A11

gaps.justification: Spawn, grab, pin and delete are the playground's editor modes over VisualCore's recognizers, GestureArbiter and SceneNode.hitTest, with native controls as the alternative; no new generic gesture is needed.
gaps.test: Host tests: tap spawns the chosen body at the touch point, drag grabs the hit body with a bounded grab force and releases with its velocity, pin fixes a body, delete removes it, every action has a control alternative (GestureAlternatives.missing is empty) and is recorded as a replayable command

gaps.justification: Velocity and force arrows, plots of measured quantities and the measured state panel with units are the playground's views over Primitive lines, polylines and polygons and native SwiftUI controls; no chart component is needed for version 0.1.
gaps.test: Host tests: arrows scale with the measured vector within caps and vanish when switched off, panel values (speed, kinetic and potential energy, spring extension) match the world state with stated units, overlays never change the state digest, the spoken summary is rate-limited

gaps.justification: The pendulum, spring chain and stacked-objects presets and the saved-experiment document are the playground's content stored in ExperienceStorage through VisualCorePersistence (clarification 5); they run on G-CONTACTS and G-SPRINGS.
gaps.test: Host tests: each preset loads, runs deterministically and resets to its document; the pendulum's period and the chain's rest shape match stated tolerances; saved experiments round-trip, a write interrupted mid-way keeps the previous file, damaged or newer files are reported and never crash

gaps.justification: The body budget, caps on contacts, constraints, speeds and stiffness per quality tier, sleeping bodies and the clamp-or-refuse policy for an experiment that would become unstable are the playground's policy over the solver's own bounds (clarification 5).
gaps.test: Host tests: spawning beyond the body budget is refused with a message, speeds and stiffness stay within caps, resting bodies fall asleep and wake on contact or grab, an extreme experiment is clamped or refused and never produces a non-finite value; per-step work stays within the arithmetic bound for the budget

gaps.justification: Per-content author and license fields for presets, palettes and shaders belong to the experience's content definitions (as Neon Arcade's LicenseAudit); the audit starts with the first bundled content in A11-P01 and covers the presets added in A11-P04. Built in A11-P01: MaterialCatalog (four MIT materials with a validating decoder) and LicenseAudit, which generates docs/apps/physics-playground/content-licenses.md.
gaps.test: Host tests: every bundled preset, palette and shader records an author and a license and the audit fails on a missing one

gaps.justification: Split from G-CONTACTS at A11-P01: a broad phase (pairs equal to brute force, fewer narrow-phase tests) and resting-stack stability (warm starting or equivalent positional handling so a stack of boxes stays bounded) are generic and belong to VisualCoreSimulation; A11-P01 tests all pairs of at most 48 bodies. Built in A11-P02: AABB2D, Shape2D.bounds(at:), BroadPhase2D.pairs (sweep and prune, equal to brute force) and warm starting (Contact2D stored impulses, inout ImpulseSolver2D.solve); a five-box stack drifts 0.8 mm and sinks 1.4 mm over 10 s.
gaps.test: Host tests (BroadPhase2DTests, 7 tests; ImpulseSolver2DTests): broad phase equals brute force on 50 seeded scenes; cold start bit-identical to Phase 01; five-box stack drift < 2 cm and sink < 1 cm over 1,200 ticks; API baseline additive; reference regression at X-A11

reasons: A working host and drawing path exist: RenderHost on OpenGL ES -> ANGLE -> Metal and PrimitiveRenderer drawing a SceneNode tree of rectangles, circles, lines, polygons and polylines in one batch through Camera2D, all public and tested.

9 of 18 rows are available with tests: scene rendering, geometry, animation, shader-based effects, fixed step and step policy, persistence, quality tiers and low power, accessibility and Reduce Motion, lifecycle; the deterministic base (FixedStepRunner with pause and stepOnce, TimeStepPolicy, SeededRandom, StateDigest, Collision2D) is in place.

All gaps are additive and owned: G-CONTACTS (box contacts, impulse solver with restitution, friction and positional correction, broad phase) and G-SPRINGS (spring constraints with bounded stiffness), both VisualCoreSimulation upstream in A11-P02; app-local G-RIGIDBODY (body and world model, units, static bodies, gravity, drag, integration, pause, single step, time scale, reset) and G-CONTENTLICENSES in A11-P01, G-EDITOR and G-OVERLAYS in A11-P03, G-EXPERIMENTS in A11-P04, G-STABILITY in A11-P05.

No permission and no privacy answer changes; Physics Playground stays unregistered until A11-P01 creates Packages/ExperiencesCreative/PhysicsPlayground with its targets and first real rules, so the experience package check and the one app are unchanged.
